newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bombay prepares for funeral of riot dead.
newsitem.headline: India's Bombay prepares for funeral of riot dead.

text.p: India's commercial capital was tense on Sunday but slowly limping back to normal after a day's strike as authorities prepared for the funeral of 10 people shot dead during a riot, police said.
"We have the situation under control," a police spokesman told Reuters. "But there are some pockets which are tense."

Angry mobs forced shops and businesses in Bombay to shut down on Saturday, a day after police fired on a crowd in a suburb of the city, killing 10. Friday's riot had erupted after a garland of shoes was placed on the statue of a revered leader of the lower social classes. Protesters, reacting to what they said was a serious insult, blocked roads and railway tracks on Saturday and threw stones at vehicles defying the protest strike. Life in the bustling metropolis of 13 million people ground to a halt.

The suburban trains which form Bombay's lifeline were stopped after rioting crowds threw stones at them. Buses and private vehicles were badly damaged. The agitation also threw airline schedules out of gear.
On Sunday, transport services paralysed by the strike were gradually returning to normal, officials said. Shops and markets opened briefly for people to stock up on essential commodities.

Paramilitary troops in riot gear lined the streets of the northeastern suburb of Ghatkopar, 15 km (9 miles) from the city, as huge crowds gathered for a funeral march for the 10 people who died there.
The mob was protesting against the desecration of the statue of Bhimrao Ambedkar, a lawyer who helped draft India's constitution and was a dynamic leader of India's lower castes, police said.
Police dispersed some protesters who tried to erect road blocks at Akola, about 500 km (313 miles) northeast of Bombay.
"Police were able to disperse the crowd without force," the spokesman said.
Opposition parties who called Saturday's strike in the city have called another one on Monday in the rest of the western state of Maharashtra, where Bombay is located.
But Bombay, where one person was killed in police firing on Saturday, would be exempted from Monday's strike, police said.
The Maharashtra government has ordered a judicial probe into the cause of the shooting.
